## Purpose and entry points
DeskcommCRM is a self-hostable, multi-tenant sales CRM centered on WhatsApp operations, with human attendants and AI agents sharing inbox, pipeline, and automation workflows. The Next.js App Router serves public auth, authenticated tenant UI, platform-admin UI, REST APIs, webhooks, cron endpoints, and MCP endpoints. Primary roots: `app/layout.tsx`, `app/app/layout.tsx`, `app/api/v1/`, `app/admin/(protected)/`.

## Tenant security and persistence boundary
Supabase provides Postgres, Auth, Storage, Realtime, pgvector, and the tenant-isolation boundary through RLS. Server/browser/admin clients are separated in `lib/supabase/server.ts`, `lib/supabase/browser.ts`, and `lib/supabase/admin.ts`. The installable schema baseline is `supabase/baseline.sql`; incremental domain changes live in `supabase/migrations/`, including AI agents and follow-up flows. Authorization helpers enforce role and platform-admin boundaries in `lib/auth/require-role.ts` and `lib/auth/requirePlatformAdmin.ts`.

## CRM and live-attendance core
The tenant application exposes Inbox, Contacts, Kanban/pipelines, team management, metrics, audit, settings, and LGPD operations under `app/app/`. Canonical business APIs are route handlers under `app/api/v1/conversations/`, `app/api/v1/leads/`, and `app/api/v1/contacts/`. Inbox operations include sending messages, assignment/claim/release/transfer, notes, snoozing, media, and retention; React clients use realtime-oriented hooks such as `hooks/inbox/useConversationsRealtime.ts` and `hooks/inbox/useMessagesRealtime.ts`.

## Channels and message lifecycle
Channel adapters normalize WAHA and Meta Cloud WhatsApp behind `lib/channels/index.ts`, with implementations in `lib/channels/adapters/waha.ts` and `lib/channels/adapters/meta-cloud.ts`. Inbound provider webhooks enter through `app/api/v1/webhooks/waha/[token]/route.ts` or `app/api/v1/webhooks/meta/[token]/route.ts`, are validated/ingested, persisted as CRM conversations/messages, and become realtime-visible. Outbound messaging is mediated by messaging APIs and channel capability/pacing controls; media derives, persistence, transcription, and cleanup are handled by `workers/media-persist-worker.ts`, `workers/media-derive-worker.ts`, and `workers/storage-cleanup-worker.ts`.

## AI-agent runtime and knowledge
The AI module configures versioned agents, credentials, providers, budgets, skills, routers, cases, memory, and RAG through `app/api/v1/ai/` and the operator UI in `app/app/ai/`. The execution engine is centered in `lib/agent-engine/agent/inbound-turn.ts`, `lib/agent-engine/agent/resolve-turn-agent.ts`, and `workers/agent-worker/main.ts`: an inbound turn resolves an eligible agent, gathers CRM/knowledge context, invokes an LLM/provider, applies guardrails, and dispatches actions or a human handoff. RAG ingestion and embedding reside in `lib/ai/rag/` and `workers/rag-indexer.ts`; model calls use Vercel AI SDK-compatible provider logic in `lib/agent-engine/edge/llm/run-model-call.ts`.

## Automation, follow-ups, and asynchronous control flow
Domain events are recorded and drained rather than causing direct database-triggered HTTP calls. `lib/event-log/drain.ts` and `app/api/v1/cron/event-log-drain/route.ts` feed the automation engine in `lib/automation/engine.ts`. Public tenant capture webhooks enter at `app/api/v1/webhooks/in/[token]/route.ts`; rules can mutate CRM state, send WhatsApp, or invoke outbound webhooks. Follow-up graphs are authored in `app/app/ai/followups/[id]/`, validated/published by `lib/followup/publish.ts`, and executed by `lib/followup/engine.ts` via `app/api/v1/cron/followup-flow-worker/route.ts`. Routing, snooze, risk, LGPD, and agent dispatch have comparable cron/worker boundaries under `app/api/v1/cron/` and `workers/`.

## Governance, integrations, and deployment
Guardrails constrain AI sends, disclosure, LGPD basis, messaging windows, and promises in `lib/agent-engine/guardrails/`; auditing is centralized in `lib/audit/index.ts`. MCP exposes governed CRM tools through `app/api/mcp/route.ts` and `lib/mcp/server.ts`. Nuvemshop OAuth/webhooks are isolated in `lib/nuvemshop/` and `app/api/v1/webhooks/nuvemshop/`. Runtime is Node 22, Next.js 16/React 19, TypeScript, and Docker; `Dockerfile` runs the application while `Dockerfile.worker` supports worker execution. Deployment options include Vercel plus a WhatsApp VPS, or the self-host stack orchestrated by `docker-compose.yml` and `hostgator-setup-kit/install.sh`. External services include Supabase, WAHA, AI providers/AI Gateway, Upstash Redis, Resend, Sentry, and Nuvemshop.
